newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to speed up mining approvals.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to speed up mining approvals.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Thursday ordered the Department of Environment and Natural Resources to "fast track" applications of foreign companies for mining licences in the country.
"Those that deserve to be approved, let's approve them so that they can get into the act," Ramos said at the launching of a Presidential award for firms that promote protection of the environment.
The government's approval of a new mining law allowing foreign firms 100 percent in local mining projects has attracted 20 of the biggest names in industry, Ramos said.

The Philippine has so far approved the applications of Western Mining Corp and Arimco for financial and technical assistance agreements (FTAA) and 60 other mineral products sharing agreements (MPSA) involving joint ventures between local and foreign firms.
There are 120 more FTAA and 1,500 MPSA applications waiting for approvals at the DENR.
Ramos said protection of the environment and tribal landowners had been strenghtened with the approval of revisions to the implementing rules and regulations (IRR) to the mining law late last year.
The revisions were made after tonnes of waste from a mine run by Marcopper Mining Corp, a unit of Placer Dome Inc, in the central Philippines leaked into a nearby river in March 1996.
The accident raised concerns over the effects liberalisation was having on the mining industry.
The revisions on the implementing rules will also protect the country from mere speculators, Ramos said.
"By requiring stronger financial qualifications, the IRR has also shut the door of mining business to speculators and incompetent mining contractors," Ramos said.
